For the past 30 years, descendants of Jewish art collectors whose works were looted by the Nazis during World War II have sought to reclaim stolen works of art.

On Tuesday, the Art Institute of Chicago announced it is returning a 1913 painting, “Woman with a Fan” by Jean Metzinger, to the heirs of its original owner.

“What is significant here is our research confirms the painting was owned by the Lewenstein family, a Jewish family who lived in Amsterdam, and that the painting was sold in a forced sale in 1940 in Nazi-occupied Amsterdam,” said Jacques Schuhmacher, executive director of provenance research at the museum.

Experiments at the National Elephant Institute in Thailand show Asian pachyderms are able to deny their impulses and choose a more rational course of action, in order to solve problems.
